# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# cogmo-devbase — base task-container image for coding-delegation.
#
# Built and published as the `devbase` target of `/docker-bake.hcl` by
# .github/workflows/publish.yml at every cogmo release. Tag tracks the
# cogmo app version, so `cogmo:1.46.0` always pairs with
# `cogmo-devbase:1.46.0`. See design/coding-delegation.md → "Base Image"
# for the full contract.
#
# Today's image ships what plan-only Claude Code flows need plus the uv
# toolchain skill-authoring tasks rely on (`uv pip compile` to produce a
# `requirements.lock` byte-identical to what `cogmo-skills` resolves at
# register time):
#   - Node 24 + pnpm + git + gh + ripgrep + fd + jq + curl
#   - @anthropic-ai/claude-code (pinned)
#   - Python 3 (from devcontainers/base) + uv (pinned to match cogmo-skills)
#   - Non-root user `vscode` (UID 1000) inherited from the devcontainers base.
#
# Codex CLI and Go/Rust toolchains are deferred to whenever real verify
# commands need them.

# uv as a stage, shared with cogmo-skills. Defaults are the standalone-build
# fallback; docker-bake.hcl overrides them for published builds and
# version-pins.test.ts enforces the match. ARG-in-FROM needs global scope.
ARG UV_VERSION=0.12.5
ARG UV_DIGEST=sha256:e85be844203885286c60ffad8a858d48afb6c5a5c237ca0e67f12e74b8f174b1
FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION}@${UV_DIGEST} AS uv

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/base:ubuntu-24.04@sha256:d94c97dd9cacf183d0a6fd12a8e87b526e9e928307674ae9c94139139c0c6eae

# Make `RUN ... | ...` fail when any element of the pipe fails. The
# nodesource install (`curl ... | bash -`) below silently succeeds on a
# truncated curl without this.
SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-o", "pipefail", "-c"]

# Toolchain versions — defaults mirror docker-bake.hcl (see the uv note above).
ARG NPM_VERSION=12.0.2
ARG PNPM_VERSION=11.21.0
ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.233

# devcontainers/base already ships git, gh, curl, jq, ripgrep — but `fd-find`
# is missing on Ubuntu and the binary is named `fdfind` rather than `fd`.
#
# `apt-get upgrade` applies Ubuntu security updates that landed after the
# upstream rebuild — the devcontainers base image trails published USN
# advisories by days to weeks and accumulates a large CVE surface on the
# `ubuntu-24.04` tag. Hadolint's DL3005 disagrees with this on the premise
# that maintainers keep base images patched; in practice they don't, and
# this image runs inside sysbox sandboxes where every patch we can apply
# at build time tightens the userland surface.
# hadolint ignore=DL3005
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get upgrade -y \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends fd-find \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
 && ln -s /usr/bin/fdfind /usr/local/bin/fd

# Node 24 LTS via NodeSource. Upgrade npm past the bundled version — its
# bundled deps (picomatch / ip-address / brace-expansion) lag upstream and
# show up as image CVEs.
RUN curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_24.x | bash - \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends nodejs \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
 && npm install -g "npm@${NPM_VERSION}" \
 && npm cache clean --force

# pnpm via npm, not corepack — corepack's cached pnpm bundle (tar /
# picomatch / minimatch / brace-expansion) lags upstream and shows up as
# image CVEs.
RUN npm install -g "pnpm@${PNPM_VERSION}" \
 && pnpm --version \
 && npm cache clean --force

# Claude Code CLI. npm blocks install scripts unless the package is named in
# `--allow-scripts`, independently of `ignore-scripts`. Claude Code ships a
# thin JS wrapper plus a per-platform native binary as an optional dependency,
# and its postinstall is what puts that binary in place — without the
# allowlist the install "succeeds" and `claude` then fails at runtime with
# "native binary not installed". Naming the one package we intend to trust
# keeps the default deny for everything else in the tree.
RUN npm install -g --allow-scripts=@anthropic-ai/claude-code "@anthropic-ai/claude-code@${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION}" \
 && claude --version \
 && npm cache clean --force

# uv — shared pin with cogmo-skills so author-side `uv pip compile` produces
# lockfiles byte-identical to what cogmo-skills re-resolves at register time.
COPY --from=uv /uv /uvx /usr/local/bin/

# Drop privileges. Cogmo's supervisor mounts the worktree at /workspace and
# always overrides Entrypoint/Cmd at create-container time, so we leave the
# image's default entrypoint alone (devcontainers/base provides one suitable
# for `docker run` smoke tests).
USER vscode
WORKDIR /workspace

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"# Task
In the skills repo, author a new skill named "btc-spot" on a new feature branch (e.g. skill/btc-spot-2026-08-18). Create two files:

1. SKILL.md — manifest with: name: btc-spot, a short description ("Fetches the current Bitcoin price in USD from CoinGecko"), tier: notify, inputs: none (empty object schema), effects: outbound network call to CoinGecko public API (read-only, no side effects). Do NOT declare any dependencies section — the skill must use only Python stdlib plus the provided ctx.http client, no third-party packages.

2. skill.py — implements:

async def run(inputs, ctx) -> dict:
    Fetches https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/simple/price?ids=bitcoin&vs_currencies=usd
    using `resp = await ctx.http.get(url)` where resp is a dict with 'status' and 'body' keys.
    Parse resp['body'] with json.loads (import json from stdlib).
    Extract the USD price at data['bitcoin']['usd'].
    Return {"price": <number>} on success.
    If resp['status'] is not 200, or the response body doesn't parse/contain the expected keys, raise a clear RuntimeError (or return an error dict per the repo's existing skill conventions — check an existing skill in the repo for the established error-handling pattern and follow it).

Do NOT use urllib, requests, httpx, or any other HTTP library — only `await ctx.http.get(url)` as described. Do NOT create a requirements.lock or any dependency manifest file for this skill. Look at an existing skill in the repo first to match file layout, SKILL.md schema, and coding conventions exactly. Push the branch when done.

# Environment
- Repo root is /workspace. Stay inside it.
- Current branch: cogmo/01a016305afb. Already created and checked out.
- Git credentials are NOT available in plan mode — you cannot push or pull.
- Do NOT make any edits. Plan only.

# Skills repo convention
- This is the skills library. One feature branch = exactly one skill.
- Place SKILL.md (the manifest), skill.py (the implementation), and (if
  the skill imports any third-party package) requirements.lock at /workspace root.
  Do NOT put them in a `skills/<name>/` subdirectory — registration reads them from the
  repo root and rejects layouts that hide them inside subdirs.
- skill.py must export `async def run(inputs, ctx) -> dict`.

SKILL.md frontmatter contract — these are validated structurally, not free-form:
  - The frontmatter is YAML. Any value containing `{`, `}`, `:`, `#`, `[`, or `]`
    MUST be wrapped in double quotes — otherwise YAML parses the special char as
    structure (e.g. unquoted `{ price: number }` becomes a nested flow mapping).
  - name: lowercase, starts with letter, [a-z0-9_-] only
  - description: 10-500 chars; quote it if it contains any YAML-special char above
  - tier: one of "wasm" | "container" (NOT "notify"/"approve" — those are risk tiers
    auto-derived from effects, not authored)
  - inputs: a JSON Schema object — must include `type: object` and (usually)
    `properties` + `required` arrays. Use `{type: object, properties: {}}` for
    no-arg skills. Never `inputs: none` or `inputs: <string>`.
  - effects: an array of strings, picked from this closed set: reads_memory,
    writes_memory, reads_user_data, writes_user_data, sends_email, sends_message,
    posts_public, deletes_external, financial, reads_filesystem, writes_filesystem,
    spawns_subprocess. Use `[]` if none apply. Never a free-form string or a value
    outside this set. A read-only HTTP call to a public API needs no effects.
  - dependencies: an array of strict `name==version` strings. Required for any
    third-party import in skill.py. Use `[]` (or omit) when skill.py is stdlib-only.

Lockfile contract — if dependencies is non-empty:
- Generate requirements.lock with `uv pip compile --no-header --generate-hashes
  -o requirements.lock -` reading specs from stdin, e.g.:
    `printf 'httpx==0.27.2\n' | uv pip compile --no-header --generate-hashes
    -o requirements.lock -`
  uv is on PATH in the sandbox. The lockfile resolves transitive deps with
  hashes — register byte-compares against a fresh re-resolve, so `--no-header`
  is required (the header is non-deterministic).

Minimal valid SKILL.md (no deps):
```
---
name: example-skill
description: "One-line summary of what the skill does (at least 10 chars)."
tier: wasm
inputs:
  type: object
  properties: {}
effects: []
---
Free-form markdown body describing the skill in more detail.
```

Same shape with dependencies + a description that contains YAML-special chars:
```
---
name: example-skill
description: "Fetches the current BTC price and returns { price: number }."
tier: wasm
inputs:
  type: object
  properties: {}
effects: []
dependencies:
  - "httpx==0.27.2"
---
```

# Verify command (for context — runs after execution, not during plan)
true

# Budget
Aim to keep the task within ~200000 tokens of execution. If the task is too large, narrow scope rather than promise the moon.

# When finished
Produce a "## Plan" section describing the steps you would take, the files you would touch, and how you would verify. Cogmo posts this plan to the human for approval before any execution. No edits, no commits, no pushes."}}
